messages.subject: mqmpermutation
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,
I have troubles using the mqmpermutation function :
First, as a trial I've run this function to get a LOD threshold based
on 10 permutations. Why does it return a list containing 11 elements
and not 10 as the number of permutations was ?

Second, I'd like to use the results of mqmpermutation in
summary.scanone() but it seems it doesn't work as previously. Indeed,
with previous Rqtl version, it was possible to get a summary of a
scanone object showing the significant chormosome positions based on
the threshold calculated using permutations. As an example :
result <- scanone(data)
permut <- scanone(data, n.perm=1000)
summary(result, perms=permut, alpha=0.05)

Using the add-on MQM functions, It would be something like :

data <- mqmaugment(data, minprob = 0.1, verbose = TRUE)
setcofactors <- mqmsetcofactors(data, 5)

phencol <- find.pheno(data, trait)
mqm_backw <- mqmscan(augmentedcross, cofactors=setcofactors,
pheno.col= phencol,
step.size=5, step.max=500)
operm.mqm <- mqmpermutation(cross=data, scanfunction=mqmscan,
pheno.col=phencol,
	           n.perm=1000, method=c("permutation"),
cofactors=setcofactors, step.max=500)

tempo <- mqmprocesspermutation(operm.mqm)
tempo <- summary(mqm_backw, perms=tempo, alpha=0.05, pvalues=TRUE)

This last command gives an error message telling :
"In summary.scanone(mqm_backw, perms = tempo, alpha = 0.05, pvalues =
TRUE) :
  Just one column of permutation results; reusing for all LOD score
columns."

So what's wrong ? Does that mean it applies the threshold to both LOD
and LOD*info columns ?

Last point: it seems that while the argument phen.col works well in
mqmscan(), It seems not to be the case for mqmpermuation: it always
takes the first phenotype as by default.

Thanks in advance for your help and your attention.

PS : I can provide source files and commands if needed.

messages.body_plain:
On Jul 15, 2010, at 8:18 AM, MBogard wrote:

> Dear all,
> I have troubles using the mqmpermutation function :
> First, as a trial I've run this function to get a LOD threshold based
> on 10 permutations. Why does it return a list containing 11 elements
> and not 10 as the number of permutations was ?

The result of mqmpermutation is a list; the first element is the result with the data not being permuted.  The subsequent results are for each of the permutations.

> Second, I'd like to use the results of mqmpermutation in
> summary.scanone() but it seems it doesn't work as previously. Indeed,
> with previous Rqtl version, it was possible to get a summary of a
> scanone object showing the significant chormosome positions based on
> the threshold calculated using permutations. As an example :
> result <- scanone(data)
> permut <- scanone(data, n.perm=1000)
> summary(result, perms=permut, alpha=0.05)
>
> Using the add-on MQM functions, It would be something like :
>
> data <- mqmaugment(data, minprob = 0.1, verbose = TRUE)
> setcofactors <- mqmsetcofactors(data, 5)
>
> phencol <- find.pheno(data, trait)
> mqm_backw <- mqmscan(augmentedcross, cofactors=setcofactors,
> pheno.col= phencol,
> step.size=5, step.max=500)
> operm.mqm <- mqmpermutation(cross=data, scanfunction=mqmscan,
> pheno.col=phencol,
> 	           n.perm=1000, method=c("permutation"),
> cofactors=setcofactors, step.max=500)
>
> tempo <- mqmprocesspermutation(operm.mqm)
> tempo <- summary(mqm_backw, perms=tempo, alpha=0.05, pvalues=TRUE)
>
> This last command gives an error message telling :
> "In summary.scanone(mqm_backw, perms = tempo, alpha = 0.05, pvalues =
> TRUE) :
>  Just one column of permutation results; reusing for all LOD score
> columns."
>
> So what's wrong ? Does that mean it applies the threshold to both LOD
> and LOD*info columns ?

It's not really an error, but rather just a warning.  summary.scanone is not aware that it should ignore the "info" and "LOD*info" columns in the output of mqmscan(), but notes that the output of mqmscan has three columns and the output of mqmpermutation followed by mqmprocesspermutation has one column.  The results should still be appropriate.

> Last point: it seems that while the argument phen.col works well in
> mqmscan(), It seems not to be the case for mqmpermuation: it always
> takes the first phenotype as by default.

It does seem to be working with the correct phenotype, however it gives the wrong name to the LOD column in the output.  That's a bug, and we'll fix it shortly.

Regards,
karl

messages.subject: Dropping Individuals & Fixing A<>B mis-coding
messages.body_plain:
Karl:

Two questions:

1.  If, after loading data into R/qtl, you find that you need to drop (delete) some individuals from your populations.  What, then, is the R/qtl best command set for doing that?

2.  If, after finding a couple of markers with switched A<>B coding, what simple command have you used for letter-coded genotyping?  The solution offered on page 55 of the Broman & Sen book for inverting numerically-coded genotypes of 1,2,3,- is clever, i.e.,  g[,"c1m3"] < 4 - g[,"c1m3"], but I am having a brain-block today relative to devising an equally clever R command (too little experience with R, I guess) for inverting letter-coded F2 genotypes of A,H,B,-.

Your e-mailed help on these two questions would be greatly appreciated.

- Jim

messages.body_plain:
> 1.  If, after loading data into R/qtl, you find that you need to drop (delete) some individuals from your populations.  What, then, is the R/qtl best command set for doing that?

There's a function subset.cross that you can use to select a portion of individuals or a portion of chromosomes. Do something like the following (for the case that there's a phenotype column "id" that specifies individuals.

  ind2drop <- c("A123", "A135", "A380", "A544", "A865", "A928")
  mycross <- subset(mycross, ind=is.na <http://is.na>(match(ind2drop, mycross$pheno$id)))

> 2.  If, after finding a couple of markers with switched A<>B coding, what simple command have you used for letter-coded genotyping?  The solution offered on page 55 of the Broman & Sen book for inverting numerically-coded genotypes of 1,2,3,- is clever, i.e.,  g[,"c1m3"] < 4 - g[,"c1m3"], but I am having a brain-block today relative to devising an equally clever R command (too little experience with R, I guess) for inverting letter-coded F2 genotypes of A,H,B,-.

The genotype codes become 1, 2, 3, once the data are loaded into R, and so "4 - genotype" replaces 1,2,3 with 3,2,1, since 4-1=3, 4-2=2 and 4-3=1.

In the development version of R/qtl (available at http://www.rqtl.org/download), there's a function switchAlleles() to do this.  I wish I'd thought of it before the book was published.

  mycross <- switchAlleles(mycross, "amarkername")

karl

messages.subject: permutation using CIM
messages.body_plain:
Dear Rqtl users,
I run a permutation procedure using the cim() function but obtained
strange results. Actually, I get 90% of the LOD score values < 5 and
about 10% > 250 ! So, when asking for a LOD threshold for alpha =
0.05, I get about 250 and all the previously detected QTL appear non
significant.
I guess having so much LOD > 250 is unlikely as well as having a non
continuous distribution (there's no intermediate values between 5 and
250) Have anyone experienced such strange results ?
This may come from my dataset so I can provide the source files if
needed .
Thanks for your help
Matthieu

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] permutation using CIM
messages.body_plain:
This is probably the case of spurious peaks that occurs with standard interval mapping when the phenotype is not very normally distributed and there are regions of low genotype information (e.g., big gaps between markers).  (See, for example, Fig 4.14 on page 97 in Broman and Sen, A guide to QTL mapping with R/qtl.)

The simplest solution is to use method="hk" (Haley-Knott regression) and/or transform the phenotype, perhaps by taking ranks and then converting to normal quantiles.

Here's a function to do the latter:

  nqrank <- function(x)
    {
      y <- rank(x[!is.na <http://is.na>(x)])
      x[!is.na <http://is.na>(x)] <- qnorm((y-0.5)/length(y))
      x
    }

then try

mycross <- transformPheno(mycross, pheno.col=1, transf=nqrank)

karl

messages.subject: R/qtl version 1.17-39
messages.body_plain:
A new version of R/qtl (1.17-39) has been released at its web site
(http://www.rqtl.org).  It should be on CRAN within a couple of days.

See http://www.rqtl.org/STATUS.txt for a list of changes.  The major
changes are below.

Karl Broman
kbr...@biostat.wisc.edu

------

Version 1.17, 7/28/2010:

Major changes:

  Implemented the fit of models for binary traits in fitqtl(), by
  Haley-Knott regression and multiple imputation.  This model can also
  be used in refineqtl, scanqtl, addqtl, addpair, addint, stepwiseqtl,
  and addcovarint.

  Implemented Haley-Knott regression for binary traits in scanone and
  scantwo.

  In mqmscan(), replaced the arguments step.min and step.max with
  a single argument, off.end (to be more like scanone).

  Added functions for the joint analysis of multiple crosses, in order
  to map QTL to a phylogenetic tree.  (A paper describing the methods
  is in preparation.)  The key function is scanPhyloQTL.  simPhyloQTL
  is used to simulate data.  plot.scanPhyloQTL, max.scanPhyloQTL, and
  summary.scanPhyloQTL are the plot, max, and summary functions for
  the output from scanPhyloQTL.

messages.subject: R/qtl drop.markers command
messages.body_plain:
Karl:

I have an F2 soybean plant population (mating number p1076) that was selectively genotyped with 557 SNP markers.  I used the below two commands for the purpose of identifying markers in p1076 with segregation distortion that need to be dropped.

gt <- geno.table(p1076)
gt[ gt$p.value < 1e-4, ]

For this p1076 F2 population, R/qtl provided me with a list of 15 markers whose P values for segregation distortion ranged from 2.2e-5 to 9..7e-9.

The following command (as noted in the R/qtl manual) could be used to delete all of these markers, though I would have to specify the names of each of the 15 SNP markers (in quotes).

p1076D <- drop.markers(p1076, c("S14302","S20031","S18459","etc for 12 more markers"))

Typing each marker name with quotes into the above command is a bit tedious, given that I have 47 more such F2 populations for which I need to do the same kind of segregation distorion analysis.  Indeed, I am trying to come up with a batch file of in-common R/qtl commands to use with all 48 populations, wherein I would only have to change the pXXXX designation in the batchfile command set to make it work for any given population.

I am new to R and have not yet learned enough to be able to devise a simple command to tie the drop.markers command to the table of outputted marker names.  Thus, my question:

Do you know of a simple derivative R or R/qtl command wherein I could delete all 15 markers from p1076 by using some sort of command reference to this R/qtl outputted tabular list of 15 markers?

Any help you can provide me with regard to such a command would be greatly appreciated.

- Jim
